_comment: Reviewed names for styles-v1.json (overrides the heuristic suggestions). Keys: format -> style index. Based on the pooled stats in docs/STYLES.md and the stack-depth check (short-stackers play most hands under 25bb).

0: Plays half its hands (VPIP 48%), limps 28% yet still raises 18%, and opens almost as wide from early position (18%) as the button (32%).
1: Limps into ~4 in 10 pots and almost never raises (PFR 4%); a classic recreational caller.
2: Plays a third of hands, mostly by limping or calling; raises rarely.
3: Raises a lot but opens nearly as wide early as late (21% vs 36%): aggressive without positional discipline.
4: A bit too loose and still limps 13% of the time; middle of the pool.
5: Solid regular: tight, raises first in, widens strongly on the button (16% early vs 40% button), 3-bets 7%.
6: Tight and straightforward; slightly less aggressive than the TAG and folds to c-bets the most.
7: Push/fold short-stack strategy: 69% of hands under 25bb, raises nearly every hand it plays, 3-bets 10%, goes to showdown 43%.

0: Loosest full-ring group; limps often and raises little.
1: Almost never raises (PFR 3%); limps a quarter of hands.
2: Plays few hands and mostly passively; folds to pressure.
3: Tight-aggressive regular with real positional awareness (10% early vs 35% button).
4: Very tight and fairly passive preflop.
5: Push/fold short stack: 87% of hands under 25bb, VPIP equals PFR.

0: Opens 86% of buttons and 3-bets 19%: maximum pressure.
1: Limps the button 68% of the time instead of raising.
2: Mixes limps (28%) and raises; plays many hands but without much pressure.
3: Standard heads-up regular: opens 66% of buttons, rarely limps, 3-bets 16%.
